Len Coleman was just outside, and we had five men in the first eight places. We had hoped that Don Brown would beat A.
In the Invitation 2 Miles Walk, the Belgrave boys gave the fair sized crowd a good example of the heel and toe “stuff” and Don Brown walked in his best style to beat A.

Churcher is the first name mentioned, and his classic race with Mikaelsson (Sweden) in 1937 (when Harry returned the fastest time done by an Englishman in the Championships) is cited as proof of his ability on the track. The distance may prove too far for A.

The return match with the Police was marked by the appearance of so many middle distance men; no fewer than seven Belgrave men ran in the mile, which was won by Arthur Cooper, T.V.H., running for Belgrave.

Elected Road Captain at the next AGM - no mean feat for one so young - he led by example in both inter-club and Open events and gained his Surrey colours. The next year he improved to second place in the AAA's two miles behind the great A.
